For alignment, I’ll propose weekly syncs, shared BI workspaces for consistent data, and maintain accept criteria and review processes. I'll create a "Unified Analytics" epic using the current ticketing system and break it down into sub-epics for various teams, such as Data, Backend, Frontend, Design/UX, and Ops. Each ticket will need an assigned owner, and we'll adopt a weekly sprint cadence with planning on Mondays and reviews on Fridays. Plan in brief: create a "Unified Analytics" epic in our existing ticketing system with sub‑epics for Data, Backend, Frontend, Design/UX, and Ops, use a lightweight Kanban (To Do / In Progress / Blocked / Ready for QA / Done), require one owner per ticket, and run a weekly sprint cadence (Mon planning / Fri review).  
Alignment rules: treat the design library and BI workspace as single sources of truth, attach clear acceptance criteria (data contract, UX spec, test cases) to every ticket, require designers on visual/UX PRs, and run two 30‑minute recurring syncs (Mon planning + Wed unblock) plus ad‑hoc blocker triage using a "blocker" label.  
Tool assessment: current stack (ticketing, BI workspace, design system, staging warehouse, CI) is sufficient for now — to address Samir’s manual schema validation/test data steps we will add in‑repo Python utilities and CI jobs to automate validation and seeded test data (no new vendor purchase).  
Watchlist & triggers: if by end of week 4 we still see >3 blocking schema/data incidents or the in‑house automation requires >3 developer‑days, I will evaluate commercial schema/DBT tooling, data‑observability, or test data services and present cost/benefit options (any single purchase over my approval cap will be escalated to Elena/Jordan).  
Immediate actions I’ll take today: create the epic and project board, assign Samir/Lee/Maya as sub‑epic owners, open tickets for CI‑based schema/test‑data automation, post this plan to the kickoff thread, and schedule the recurring syncs — please flag objections within 24 hours.

Process tweak 1 (protect capacity): reserve 8 dev‑hrs per sprint as a "data‑plumbing" buffer enforced by a single "data‑plumbing‑buffer" ticket so non‑milestone work can’t consume that allocation.  
Process tweak 2 (legacy REQs): run a focused half‑day REQ‑cleanup before the milestone (owner: Lee) to batch‑map legacy Sales asks into REQs with acceptance criteria and tag anything unresolved as "deferred" to stop scope bleed.  
Process tweak 3 (planning gate): add a "milestone‑critical" label and require the REQ checklist (BI view link + design file + acceptance criteria) for any ticket to enter sprint planning; tickets missing the checklist will be blocked until complete.  
Monitoring: I’ll track effects via the weekly Manual Schema/Test‑data summary and Req Health widget at Monday syncs and will escalate (per our rules) if manual hours jump >50% week‑over‑week or if watchlist thresholds persist for two consecutive weeks.

rounds.consequence: Your capacity buffer ticket, half-day REQ cleanup, and milestone-critical labeling rules were implemented on the board.
